item.title: November 13, 2026: v3.5.103
item.description:
New features:

  • (Settings) An Integer or Decimal custom field can be computed from a formula over the record’s own numbers and its Findings’ counts, on Findings, Tests, Engagements, Assets, Organizations and Risk Acceptances. DefectDojo keeps the value up to date, and it shows read-only on the record with its formula. The Triage Engine’s Set a Custom Field node takes the same formulas. See Computed fields.
  • (Triage Engine) The Merge Findings node merges the active Findings in each Asset that share a Hash Code, Title, Vulnerability ID or Unique ID From Tool into one, keeping the oldest, newest or most severe. See Merge Findings.
  • (Permissions) With Group Ownership on, webhook receivers, notification webhooks, Downstream Connectors and ticket templates can belong to a Group, and a Group’s automation identity can hold an API token that is issued and revoked from the Group’s page. Dashboards, page layouts and saved table views can belong to a Group or be shared with chosen Groups. With Restrict Layout Customization on, a user picks from an approved set of dashboards: the instance default, the dashboards published to everyone and those their Groups own or were given. See The group’s API token, Connectors and ticket templates a Group owns, Notification webhooks a Group owns and Sharing, cloning, and defaults.
  • (Connectors) An admin can stop a running connector sync with Stop Sync on the connection’s records page. The connector pages show when a sync is stopping or was stopped, by whom, and when a sync is still importing, finished without closing Findings, or lost its worker. A Connector Health Warning goes out when a sync runs far too long, finishes without closing the Findings the tool no longer reports, stops completing for days, or is refused by the license. See Sync Operations and Getting told when a Connector stops working.
  • (Notifications) An Asset’s gear menu sets your notifications for that one Asset. See Receive Personal notifications for a specific Asset.

Enhancements:

  • (Connectors) An Azure DevOps Boards Issue Tracker Mapping has a Work Item Type: Issue, Bug, Task or a custom type. Saving a connector cancels only that connector’s running Discover or Sync, and only when the change affects it, and the edit page asks before a save cancels a run. With One Finding per Vulnerability grouping on, connector syncs fold Findings the way imports do. See Sync Operations and Deduplication Tuning.
  • (Findings) The Findings list has an SLA Status filter (Breached or Within SLA). Combined with the SLA filter, it lists Findings due soon without the overdue ones. See Findings due soon, without the overdue ones.
  • (Threat Intelligence) Every vulnerability ID has a page showing what the threat intelligence feed knows about it: exploit maturity, CISA KEV status and the evidence behind each rating, even when no Finding carries the ID. Findings, the Known Exploited mark and search link to it. The Vulnerability Explorer has Exploit Maturity and PoC Count columns, and the Findings API returns each Finding’s threat intelligence score, with its evidence on request. See Threat Intelligence and Viewing KEV/EPSS in the Vulnerability Explorer.
  • (Reporting) Every Insights page can be filtered by Test Type and Test Type Category. See Filtering.
  • (Authentication) The Pro UI warns before a session expires, with a countdown. Stay Signed In extends a session that inactivity would end. See Session expiry.
  • (Risk Acceptance) With Risk Acceptances 2.0 on (off by default), a standing acceptance can cover every Finding in an Engagement, Asset or Organization, including Findings later scans bring, with an explicit opt-in. See Every New Finding in an Asset.
  • (AI) AI Guardrails checks Gemini CLI, Windsurf and Kiro hooks against the same policies as the other agents. See AI Guardrails.
  • (Dashboards) The Scan Cadence widget shows status counts and lists overdue and never-scanned Assets. My Work is one queue. PSIRT Exposure is a share bar with filtered links. Chart widgets order and color their series consistently and fit every tile size. See Scan cadence policies, The widget catalog and PSIRT dashboard.
  • (Engagements) On the Engagement page, the Tests widget fits its tile at every size, Finding Severity by Test is a table of counts for every Test, the checklist widget is redesigned, and the Questionnaires widget lists the Engagement’s questionnaires with their actions. See Finding Severity by Test, Engagement Checklists and Questionnaires.
  • (Tests) On the Test page, Import History is a newest-first timeline, the Findings and Finding Groups widgets fit their tiles, Active Finding Severity shows what the latest import changed, and Matching Policy links to its configuration. See Working with Import History and Customizing Page Layouts.
  • (Findings) On the Finding page, Request / Response Pairs are rows that open in place, and Add Request/Response Pair in the gear menu adds the first one. The Files widget lists files by name with Add File, the Notes widget is a divided list with folded notes, and several smaller widgets are tidied. See Additional Details and How to Attach a File to a Finding.
  • (Organizations) The Organization page’s Members and Groups widgets are lists that can add, edit and remove members and Groups. Its description renders as Markdown. See Organization View.
  • (UI) The CSV export, Triage Engine and widget field pickers group fields under the same headings as Add Filter. The rule, parser and field mapping editors warn before leaving with unsaved changes. List cells show the first value and a +N chip. A refused save shows one message with the server’s reason. See Filter Index.
  • (API) Downstream Connector mappings, assignments and ticket templates can be managed on /api/v2/downstream/ with an API token. The Test import history API takes ?summary=true. See Downstream Connectors.
  • (Performance) Imports and connector syncs create new Findings in bulk. Reimport no longer loads closed Findings. Deduplication, Findings API pages with duplicates, quick search, adding a tag to a Finding, Risk Acceptance changes, report schedules, the audit log, View page tiles and CSV, JSON and XLSX exports are faster, and exports use less memory.

Bug fixes:

  • (Importers) Imports and reimports into the same Test run one at a time, so a retried reimport waits instead of failing. An SBOM imported with Import Scan or Reimport Scan records its components as Dependencies on the Asset. The import preview counts the identity-signature and cross-tool matches the import makes, and returns a result under the legacy deduplication algorithm. On reimport, false positive history stays on its own host, and a still-reported suppressed Finding stays open. See One Import at a time into a Test and Findings on different hosts.
  • (Triage Engine) A rule that closes a Finding mitigates its Endpoint statuses. Set a Field lists the instance’s own Asset types and options. Accepting or removing risk from a rule no longer posts a note to linked tickets for each Finding. Rules adopted from older templates raise the alert their template describes. See Set Status and Set a Field.
  • (Risk Acceptance) Approving an acceptance leaves out Findings closed while it waited. The upgrade releases Findings that a rule closed while they stayed risk accepted, and fills in the history of acceptances made before 3.3.0. See The record of what was accepted.
  • (Findings) Platform and Lifecycle filters match a value that contains a comma. A Finding cannot be marked a duplicate of itself or of its own cluster. All Components rows open the Findings with exactly that component name. Editing a Finding’s tags no longer fails when another request deletes a tag. The Prioritization Engine’s severity table uses the Reachability and Correlation multipliers. See Filtering findings by Platform and Finding Multipliers.
  • (Locations) Location references follow their Finding when it is closed or reopened. Sensor Coverage marks identifiers that a different sensor reports. See References.
  • (Deduplication) A Dedupe Pool reset re-scores reachability for both clusters, and a failed preview shows the server’s reason. See Dedupe Pools.
  • (Jira) A classic Jira project can turn off SLA notification comments. Text after a one-line {code} or {quote} block in a Jira comment is kept. Migrating to the Jira Downstream Connector reports each template comparison it disables. See Send SLA Notifications As Comments and Migrating to the Jira Downstream Connector.
  • (Compliance) Users with an Organization role that allows editing can edit on the compliance and regulatory pages. Saving a criticality SLA mapping applies the new SLA to every Asset it covers. See Federal Compliance.
  • (Notifications) Asset, Organization and Engagement “added” notifications are always sent. See About Notifications & Alerts.
  • (Tables) The compliance, Risk Acceptance, Asset and survey lists apply every sort and filter they offer. Embedded picker tables hide export, bulk and row controls. See Customizing Tables.
  • (UI) Status words and Asset counts read correctly in the reader’s language. Ask Sensei tiles stay in their boxes at phone width. Long chips stay inside chip inputs. Cloud Portal messages no longer re-save on load. The sign-in, session and export pages have a main landmark for screen readers. The multi-select Any filter on a custom field matches the selected options. Form controls and buttons share one style, and the Airgapped Instance feature flag label is title-cased. See Custom Fields.

Security fixes:

  • (Authorization) Scan imports check permissions on the same Asset and Engagement the import uses. See Introduction.
  • (Hardening) The calendar pages handle filter values and event titles safely. The Go services are built with a Go release that includes the latest security fixes.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Deployment) Imports and reimports into one Test run one at a time. DD_SERIALIZE_TEST_IMPORTS_WAIT_SECONDS (default 600) sets how long a request waits, and DD_SERIALIZE_TEST_IMPORTS (default True) should be set to False only behind a connection pooler in transaction mode. See One Import at a time into a Test.
  • (Helm) Under Istio STRICT mTLS, the connectors pod’s init checks pass and the pod starts. django.uwsgiImport.readinessProbe.workerCheck: true turns on a readiness probe for the import pool that reaches a uwsgi worker. See Service Mesh (Istio) and DefectDojo Pro Upgrade Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

item.title: November 12, 2026: v3.5.102
item.description:
New features:

  • (Triage Engine) The On Rule Complete trigger runs a rule each time another rule finishes a successful run, so rules can run in a fixed order whatever they change. The rule sweeps its own scope, as a Manual Run does, and a failed run starts nothing. See On Rule Complete and Running rules in order.

Enhancements:

  • (Triage Engine) With Restrict Triage Engine Emails to DefectDojo Users on, a Send an Email batch also reaches recipients who can see only part of it. Each recipient gets an email that lists just the Findings, Assets or alerts they can see, with a count that matches. See Restricting recipients to DefectDojo users.
  • (AI) AI Guardrails keeps Prompt Activity for a set number of days, 90 by default, which a superuser changes on the new Settings tab. A Daily Activity chart keeps each day’s counts after the events themselves are deleted. See Prompt Activity.
  • (Connectors) When the license is refusing connector syncs, the Connections list and a connection’s records page say so and link to the License page. See Managing Operations.
  • (Performance) History tabs load faster on instances with a long audit history. Adding a tag to many Findings at once, the Tests API with Jira-linked Finding Groups or response_fields, Findings API pages that include duplicates, the Triage Engine Rules list, and the close step of a large connector sync are faster.

Bug fixes:

  • (Connectors) A large connector sync that is cut off by its time limit, a deploy or a lost worker continues where it stopped. It finishes, closes the Findings the tool no longer reports and records the sync in Import History. See Sync Operations.
  • (Triage Engine) Turning a rule on or off takes effect right away. A rule that changes Findings and then deletes them in the same run completes. A rule that sets an Organization or parent Asset by a computed name skips a name an archived Organization or Asset holds instead of failing the run. The Import Rules preview runs again when Owned By changes while a preview is running. See Runs and Importing rules.
  • (Risk Acceptance) Closing a risk-accepted Finding marks its Endpoint statuses mitigated. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Compliance) Evidence packs for an assessment that covers several Assets or a whole Organization can be generated, opened and downloaded. The CMMC Assessment page opens an Asset’s newest assessment, the same one the Asset’s Compliance summary reports. See Federal Compliance and CMMC Level 2 Assessments.
  • (Jira) A classic Jira instance whose configuration name is longer than 255 characters migrates to a Jira Downstream Connector. See Migrating to the Jira Downstream Connector.
  • (Dashboards) A Graph over a date labels each period by its size, in the reader’s language, instead of with an ISO date. A short Graph tile keeps room for its chart. The Regulatory Scope widget answers a malformed regulations value with a validation error instead of a server error. See Graph options.
  • (Findings) A Component with a blank name opens its own Findings from All Components and from the Asset’s Components widget. See Components.
  • (UI) The severity donut’s ring labels stay off its legend. The source toggle on a Markdown field no longer covers the text. A failed table preference read or Location map save shows one toast instead of several. The column filter menus on the Components and Support Requests tables show their match modes in the app language, and Dedupe Pool counts use the app language’s number format.

Security fixes:

  • (Hardening) Date filters refuse a Past Days value outside the supported range. dojo-deploy is built with a Go release that includes the latest security fixes. See Filter Index and Keeping the CLI up to date.

Behavior changes:

  • (Authentication) Nobody is asked to accept the End User License Agreement after signing in. The organization’s subscription agreement already covers its users.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Deployment) The upgrade adds indexes to the audit history tables, which can take a minute or more on an instance with millions of Findings. One read of an object’s History tab is limited by DD_OBJECT_HISTORY_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT, 30 seconds by default, and 0 leaves it only the web statement limit. See Hardware Sizing.
  • (Helm) With networkPolicy.profile: aggressive, the Celery imports worker, the OSCAL validator, the Orchestrator workers and the helm test pods get the network access they need, including to the embedded Redis. See Network Policies and DefectDojo Pro Upgrade Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

item.title: November 11, 2026: v3.5.101
item.description:
NOTE: v3.5.101 was revoked: This release shows each user a license agreement acceptance screen that was not intended. No additional agreement is required. Upgrade to v3.5.102.

NOTE: Endpoints are deprecated and will be removed in 3.7.0 on January 4, 2027.

New features:

  • (Reporting) Export Template on a Report Builder template’s row menu downloads the template with its theme, blocks and images, and Import on All Report Templates previews the file and then adds it, so a template built on a test instance can move to production. A user can delete the reports they generated. With group ownership on, a report can be generated for a Group, which renders it with the Group’s access, and a report can be shared with other Groups. See Move templates between instances and Generated reports and groups.
  • (Dashboards) The Graph widget can split its series by a second field, such as Severity Group, print values on the chart, and color each series. The KPI / Trend widget can chart open Findings at the end of each month or week, by severity or severity group. See Graph options and Open findings at each month end.
  • (Tests) Every Test Type has a category, such as SAST, DAST or SCA. Built-in scanners get one from their name, and any Test Type can be set to another on its form. Tests and Findings can be filtered by category, and dashboard charts can group scans by it. See Charting scans by category.
  • (Permissions) A custom role has an Assignable by Non-superusers setting. While it is off, only a superuser or a global Owner can give that role to a user or a Group. It is on by default, so nothing changes on upgrade. See Choosing which roles non-superusers may assign.
  • (Jira) A Jira Downstream Connector mapping can post the daily SLA notices and Risk Acceptance changes as comments on its tickets, with Post SLA Notifications as Comments and Post Risk Acceptance Changes as Comments. Both are off by default, and migrating a classic Jira project carries its settings over. See Jira.
  • (AI) AI Guardrails checks OpenAI Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot CLI hooks against the same policies as Claude Code. Rules can match the tool or MCP server a call uses, the files it touches and the commands a shell line runs, and Claude Code sends more events to check. See AI Guardrails.

Enhancements:

  • (Assets) More widgets on the Asset page fit their tile at every size. Versions leads with the newest version and its counts. Regulatory is a readiness checklist, and the profile is edited in a dialog. Engagements, Technologies, Components and Asset Identity are compact lists with their own search, and Components counts only the Asset’s Findings. Finding Severity Breakdown is a ring with a legend that counts, Reachability Coverage shows its coverage rate in the header, Regulations rows lead with the acronym, and Organization Memberships shows each membership as one row with its type and origin. Tab groups fit their tile, show how many items each tab holds and put tabs that do not fit under More. See Asset View, The Versions widget, Regulatory Profile, Components on the Asset View and Customizing Page Layouts.
  • (Settings) Settings > Defaults holds Instance Defaults and Default Profiles on one page, and every page uses the same names: Instance Default, Set as My Default and From a profile. A superuser can assign a Default Profile to one user, and assign a profile to many Groups at once with Assign to Groups. A user’s own choice comes first, then their own Default Profile, then their Groups’ profiles by rank, then the Instance Default. See Default Profiles.
  • (Reporting) A Group’s page has one Owned Content tab that counts each kind of content the Group owns and opens its list filtered to the Group. Reporting > Schedules lists report schedules, and the Owner filter on group-owned lists can pick a Group. A report schedule follows its template’s owner when the template moves. See Report schedules.
  • (Triage Engine) The Automation History widget leads with counts of changes and of sent, failed and skipped deliveries, and lists failed deliveries first. See Customizing Page Layouts.
  • (Connectors) TruffleHog gives each secret the same ID across commits, and a Fold Commits toggle reports one Finding per secret per file instead of one per commit. It is off by default.
  • (Parsers) The TruffleHog parser gives each secret the same unique_id_from_tool across commits, and DD_TRUFFLEHOG_FOLD_COMMITS folds a secret’s commits into one Finding.
  • (Findings) The Findings list has an Asset Platform filter, which dashboard widgets can use too. Every date filter offers Full Months presets: Last Full Month, or Last 3, 6 or 12 Full Months. See Asset Attribute Options and Filter Index.
  • (Navigation) The What’s New panel has a Deprecations tab that lists every feature on its way out, the release that removes it and what to use instead. See Deprecations.
  • (Performance) Filtered Asset lists, the cloud remediation preview for a Finding with many Locations, rescoring after an import on a large instance, delete notifications, and the delete preview of a very large Asset are faster. A list page whose query is cancelled or loses its connection no longer runs the query a second time.

Bug fixes:

  • (Assets) Finding Distribution splits all of the Asset’s Findings by status, and shows its ring in a tab group and at phone width. Versions without a release date are listed after the newest dated release. The Asset delete preview loads instead of failing. See Asset View.
  • (Connectors) Connector syncs no longer fail when a chunk is larger than the instance’s scan upload limit: connector chunks have their own limit, 100 MB by default. See Upload Size Limits.
  • (Deduplication) With Locations on, close old Findings, same-tool deduplication and One Finding per Vulnerability grouping include each Finding’s package in the comparison, so Findings for different packages stay separate Findings. See Deduplication Tuning.
  • (Importers) With One Finding per Vulnerability grouping on, a Finding folded from several observations keeps the file path of each observation, and a reimport keeps those file paths active.
  • (Compliance) SOC 2 CC7.2 and NIS2 7.1 count successful Triage Engine runs in the assessment period as evidence. Existing assessments show these controls as Unknown until Recompute Evidence is selected. See Certification Catalogs.
  • (Triage Engine) A true or false condition stored as 1 or 0 shows as true or false in the rule editor. See Building Rules.
  • (Authentication) The End User License Agreement can be accepted while the license is read-only. See End User License Agreement.
  • (Reporting) The Created By column on the report lists shows and sorts by the user’s name. See Report Builder.
  • (UI) A keyword search typed while a list is loading runs instead of being dropped. A custom field changed while a form loads its saved values keeps the change. The Risk filter on the Findings list shows its options and chip in the app language. A list that refuses a stale sort or filter in a link says “Request Failed” instead of “Form Validation Failed”. Client-side tables only offer filters they can apply. The severity donut’s legend stays inside its tile, and the chart cards on the Endpoint, Host and Location pages stack at phone width. See Custom Fields.

Security fixes:

  • (Authorization) The Asset delete preview requires permission to delete the Asset. See Assets.

Behavior changes:

  • (Findings) Risk Scores stay on a fixed scale from 0 to 100. A Prioritization Engine has three Risk Score Thresholds on that scale in place of its four priority thresholds, and the upgrade converts existing engines. Priority itself is unchanged. See Risk Thresholds.
  • (Triage Engine) Take Ownership of an Instance rule needs what a transfer to Instance needs: Rule Edit, Rule Add as a global role, and every node family the rule uses. Taking a rule turns it off, clears its credentials and resets its sharing, as a transfer does. See Sharing and Versions.
  • (API) /api/v2/report_themes/ returns created_by as the username instead of the user ID, as the other report endpoints do. See Report Builder API.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Deployment) Web requests that only read (GET, HEAD and OPTIONS) stop any database statement that runs past 90 seconds. Writes, imports and exports keep their limits. DD_DATABASE_WEB_READ_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT changes the read limit, and 0 gives reads the web limit again. Connector chunks have their own upload limit, DD_CONNECTORS_CHUNK_MAX_MB. See Hardware Sizing and Upload Size Limits.
  • (Compose) The Docker Compose files pass DD_V3_ORGANIZATION_NONEXCLUSIVE and DD_V3_ORGANIZATION_TYPE_ROLES to the containers, both False by default. See Organizations.
  • (Helm) New values dojo.V3OrganizationNonexclusive and dojo.V3OrganizationTypeRoles (both false) set the same Organization flags, and dojo.trufflehogFoldCommits (false) sets DD_TRUFFLEHOG_FOLD_COMMITS. An install that set these through config.extra keeps working. See Organizations and DefectDojo Pro Upgrade Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

item.title: November 9, 2026: v3.5.100
item.description:
NOTE: v3.5.100 was revoked: This release shows each user a license agreement acceptance screen that was not intended. No additional agreement is required. Upgrade to v3.5.102.

NOTE: Tool Types, Tool Configurations and API Scan Configurations are deprecated and will be removed in 3.6.0 on December 7, 2026.

New features:

  • (Permissions) Permission Audit on the All Users list adds columns for each user’s flags, Global Roles, Configuration Permissions, Organizations, Assets and Groups, with filters, sorting and CSV export. A user’s page has an Access tab that lists everything the user reaches and the role or Group that grants it, and Organizations and Assets cards where roles can be added, changed or removed. A Group’s page shows the Group’s own access in the same way. Bulk Add To and Remove From on the Users list add or remove many users at once. These are part of Access Administration, a beta feature that is on by default. View As User shows the app read-only as another user sees it, for up to an hour, with an Exit bar at the top of the page. A user administrator starts it from the user’s page, and a Group lead from a member’s row on the Group’s Members tab. It requires the View As User feature flag, off by default. See Permission Audit and Effective Access and View As User.
  • (Navigation) Sidebar Presets are named sets of hidden sidebar entries, managed under Settings > UI Defaults > Sidebar Presets. A preset only hides entries: direct links, bookmarks and the API keep working. Each user picks a preset on the User Profile page, and an administrator can share a preset and make it the instance default. The feature is on by default. See Sidebar Presets.
  • (Settings) Default Profiles give every member of a Group the same starting setup. Superusers build named profiles under Settings > UI Defaults > Default Profiles and rank them, and each Group picks one on its new Defaults tab. A member’s dashboards, page layouts, table views, sidebar preset, form configuration and landing page come from their Groups’ profiles in rank order, unless they chose their own. Restrict to Selected Layouts limits members to the layouts a profile lists, and Lock Landing Page fixes where they land. See Default Profiles.
  • (Triage Engine) A Group can own Triage Engine rules and Report Builder templates, blocks, themes and schedules, share them read-only with other Groups, or publish them to everyone. A Group’s rules and report schedules run as the Group’s own automation identity, with the Group’s access. The role editor has a Group Content table, and Settings > Unowned Content lists what a deleted Group or a departed owner left behind. Requires the Group Ownership feature flag, off by default. See Sharing and Versions and Report Builder.
  • (MCP) A Personal Data Filter card on the MCP page lets a superuser filter personal data out of MCP tool results: user fields are removed or replaced with pseudonyms, audit trails are removed, and personal data is scrubbed from free text. It is off by default. See MCP Server.
  • (Locations) Supply Chain Security can analyze each npm and PyPI package version in your inventory. The Sensei engine reads the package’s code without running it and raises alerts such as an install script added since the previous version, and alert policies decide which alerts block, warn, are monitored or are ignored. Self-hosted installs can read packages through a registry mirror. Requires the Package Analysis feature flag (beta, off by default), the Supply Chain Security flag and a Sensei license. See Supply Chain Security.

Enhancements:

  • (Assets) Four widgets on the Asset page lead with what needs attention and fit their tile at every size. Compliance shows overdue POA&M items, a missing ConMon snapshot and unmet CMMC requirements. PCI DSS Scope shows what is due on the Asset. Priority and SLA Drivers names the priority fields that are not set and shows the deadline for each severity under the SLA that applies. Exposure explains its verdict from the source that decides it, and its override and production branch are set in one Edit Exposure form. See Federal Compliance, PCI DSS Scope and Patch Clocks, Finish onboarding and Asset Exposure.
  • (Findings) The Findings list has a Mitigated By column, with a user filter and sorting, and an Exploit Evidence filter that keeps Findings with a Metasploit Module, Nuclei Template or Exploit-DB Entry in Threat Intelligence, or excludes them. The Findings export offers the Version, Build ID, Commit Hash and Branch/Tag of each Finding’s Test and Engagement. See Filter Index, Threat Intelligence and Findings.
  • (Triage Engine) Run Now of an On Dedupe Match rule in Keep Both Active mode brings in the matches deduplication made before the rule existed, such as Findings already marked duplicates while both Assets shared a Dedupe Pool. A Finding’s page has a Linked Findings tab that lists the Findings a rule linked it to, where a wrong link can be removed and restored. Automation can do the same through /api/v2/finding_links/. See On Dedupe Match.
  • (Settings) Form Configuration holds several named configurations, one of them the instance default that everyone’s forms follow. Configurations can be duplicated, and an upgrade keeps the existing configuration as the default. Single Select and Multi Select custom fields can offer an Other choice, turned on per field, that saves the text the user types. See Configuring Forms and Custom Fields.
  • (Dashboards) A Maintainer can make a collaborative dashboard layout read-only. Everyone keeps it in their layout picker, and only its owner and users who can share dashboards can change it. See Customizable Dashboards.
  • (Connectors) Tenable.io tags each Finding credentialed-scan or uncredentialed-scan from the scan of the host it was found on. The tags follow the scan, so a host scanned with credentials later gets the new tag on the next sync.
  • (Navigation) Task walkthroughs outside the Sandbox can continue past a save step without saving: Next closes the form, and later steps use a record that already exists. See In-App Walkthroughs.
  • (UI) Danger buttons and badges, error and validation text, the required-field asterisk and form field borders meet WCAG AA contrast in light and dark themes, and an invalid field keeps its red border while it is hovered or focused.
  • (Performance) Creating or updating a Risk Acceptance takes the same time for one Finding as for many, and removing Findings from it sends one notification instead of one per Finding. List exports with many columns, and saving a long IP allowlist on the Firewall Settings page, are faster. The Pro database migrations run about a third faster.

Bug fixes:

  • (Connectors) GitHub Advanced Security closes the last open Finding of an alert type once GitHub reports no open alerts of that type. StackHawk An expired session no longer fails the run, and paging stops at the last page. When connection settings are saved twice in quick succession, the later save is the one applied.
  • (Triage Engine) A rule that sets a risk-accepted Finding to false positive, out of scope or mitigated takes it out of its Risk Acceptance first, as closing it by hand does. Batched alert and email text fills in the values it names, such as the Jira issue in a Jira receiver’s alert. A condition holding a comma-separated list of values can be saved, and the condition editor shows such a list and a true or false value stored as text. Saving a rule with no name says the rule needs a name. See Node Reference and Building Rules.
  • (Deduplication) The Dedupe Pool previews count the Findings a Keep Both Active rule keeps active apart from those that become duplicates. The import and reimport previews match across the Asset’s Dedupe Pool as the import does, and count a Finding a Keep Both Active rule links as created. See Dedupe Pools.
  • (Importers) When a reimport reports a container image under a newer tag, the previous image on each matched Finding is mitigated and the new one stays active. Location History on the Finding page includes container images. See Location Drift Matching.
  • (Findings) The Remediation Center groups the Findings on a host whose remediation text names the same vendor patch into one Patch action named for that patch. See Remediation Center.
  • (Sensei) A scan where a scanner timed out or failed is marked Partial, and the Partial tag says those scanners did not complete. Suggested changes in fix pull requests show as one diff. Dynamic scans that use Nuclei run with its full template set. The Generate Threat Model button is visible on the New Threat Model page. See Sensei Reference, Dynamic Scanning (DAST) and Threat Modeling.
  • (Risk Acceptance) Deleting a Risk Acceptance pushes each Finding’s removal note to its issue tracker ticket, only for Findings that have one, and the note no longer links to the deleted Risk Acceptance. Block Self-Approval of Risk Acceptances and Require Review to Extend an Expired Risk Acceptance can be changed on the System Settings page. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Permissions) Users authorized only through Organization or Asset roles can open the Vulnerability Explorer, which lists the Findings they can see. A user whose role is on an Asset’s secondary Organization can open that Asset from the lists where it appears. See EPSS / KEV.
  • (Notifications) A user with more than one global notification row receives a Pro event on every channel any of those rows turns on. See About Notifications.
  • (Integrations) The ticket template check refuses a stray - and a comment that the integration cannot read, when the template is saved instead of when a ticket is pushed. A custom field mapping that does not fit the pushed record, such as a Finding mapping on a Finding Group tracker, is reported as a configuration error that names the field and the sources it can use.
  • (Settings) The Audit Logs list loads on instances with a very large audit history: past 10,000 entries the total reads as a lower bound, such as “10,001+”. Pages never repeat or skip an entry, and an unknown sort key answers 400 instead of a server error. A feature flag change applies on every server at once, instead of up to five minutes later. See Audit Logs.
  • (Reporting) Scheduled executive posture packs are generated instead of failing. See Command Center.
  • (Authentication) After a forced password reset or an MFA step, a user who opened a classic page lands on that page instead of the home page.
  • (API) Updating a Finding that another request deletes at the same time returns 404 instead of a server error, and the OpenAPI schema download no longer fails on an unusual version value. See DefectDojo API v2.
  • (UI) A URL in a detail table stays on one line, with the whole URL in a tooltip. An empty list tab offers its add action only when the new record would show in that tab. A refused Appearance save restores the saved colors.

Security fixes:

  • (Authentication) API token authentication follows the forced password reset rule. A SAML message addressed to another service provider is refused with a 400 response. After sign-in, an MFA step, a password change or accepting the End User License Agreement, the user is only sent to a page on the same site. See Single Sign-On.
  • (Authorization) Every Risk Acceptance read, including its notes and proof file, follows the Risk Acceptance view permission. Images in reports require view access to the Engagement, Test or Finding that holds them. API v3 includes a parent Organization’s details only for users who can view that Organization. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Hardening) The application, nginx, integration and Sensei engine images apply security updates to their bundled components, and the application image leaves out packages it does not need at runtime.

Behavior changes:

  • (Authentication) Every user accepts the End User License Agreement once, after their first sign-in on this release and again when a new version is published. Nothing else loads until they select I Agree. A user who must reset their password accepts it on the password change page. See End User License Agreement.
  • (Triage Engine) The Restrict Triage Engine Emails to DefectDojo Users feature flag is on by default. While it is on, Send an Email and the email announcement of Generate a Report reach active DefectDojo users only, and each user only gets an email whose listed items they can all see. Other addresses are refused when a rule is saved, and left out with a warning when a rule is imported. Turn the flag off to let rules email any address. Rule names no longer have to be unique: exported rules carry an ID, and an import matches existing rules on it. See Send an Email and Sharing and Versions.
  • (Settings) The hidden and required fields in Form Configuration apply to /api/v2/ writes for Findings, Engagements, Tests, Assets, Organizations and Risk Acceptances: writing a hidden field or leaving a required one empty answers 400. The instance’s API schema shows the configuration. See Configuring Forms.
  • (Engagements) The Calendar shows Interactive Engagements by default. CI/CD Engagements are shown when they are selected in the Engagement Type filter, and a link that names an Engagement Type keeps it. See Calendar.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Helm) The initializer Job’s default memory limit is 2Gi, up from 1Gi, in values.yaml and every profile. New opt-in values support a service mesh and a read-only root filesystem: securityContext.nginx.readOnlyRootFilesystem, securityContext.tmpVolume.enabled (with sizeLimit), securityContext.initContainers.runAsGroup, jobs.tests.podAnnotations and jobs.certificateGeneration.podAnnotations. See Service Mesh (Istio), Read-Only Root Filesystem and DefectDojo Pro Upgrade Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

item.title: November 2, 2026: v3.5.0
item.description:
New features:

  • (Assets) Organizations, Assets, Engagements, Tests and Findings can be archived instead of deleted. Archiving hides the record and everything under it from lists, search, dashboards, metrics, reports, the API, deduplication, reimport and Triage Engine rules, and it stops counting toward the license. Archived data is kept for 2 months by default and can be restored at any point in that period, after which it is deleted. The Archived page lists each archive, and opening one shows its records read-only in the usual lists and pages. Triage Engine rules can archive Findings on a schedule, and excess duplicates are archived instead of deleted. Self-hosted installs can change the retention period with DD_ARCHIVE_RETENTION_MONTHS. Requires the Archive feature flag, off by default. See Archive.
  • (Triage Engine) The Notifications template pack has a template that sends an in-app alert when new Findings match a set of filters: pick the filters in the trigger’s scope, and the rule sends one alert for each batch of matching Findings, however they were added. See Building Rules.
  • (Navigation) Each user can choose the page they land on after signing in, from Default Landing Page under Signing In on the User Profile page. The choice follows the account to every browser, and applies to single sign-on started from the identity provider. Controlled by the Default Landing Page feature flag, on by default. See Default Landing Page.
  • (Authentication) Idle Timeout on the Login Settings page signs a user out after a set time without a request, from 15 minutes to 8 hours. It is off by default and applies to password and SSO logins alike. See Login Settings.

Enhancements:

  • (Connectors) Security Hub can import Findings on ECR container images only for images Amazon Inspector reports in use. CrowdStrike Falcon imports Identity Protection detections. Checkmarx One can select scans by Initiator, combined with the Branch filter.
  • (Integrations) ServiceDesk Plus sends custom fields and a ticket template with each ticket, and a refused ticket shows the error ServiceDesk Plus returned.
  • (SSO) Use Mapped Username on the SAML settings page takes the username from the attribute mapped to Username instead of the NameID. It is off by default. The SAML Login Attempts panel lists the attributes received on each login, which mapping rows were found, and where the username came from. See SAML Configuration.
  • (Permissions) The All Users and All Groups tables have a Permissions column that opens a read-only grid of the permissions a user or group holds, and which Global Role grants each one. See Custom RBAC Roles.
  • (Assets) The Finding Distribution panel on the Asset page is a status ring beside a tile for each source. The record cards on the Asset page sit below the metadata row. See Assets and Customizing Page Layouts.
  • (UI) Each main list with nothing in it offers its main action, such as adding the first Asset.
  • (Performance) The Executive Insights summary, the Vulnerability Explorer list, the Assets list counts, the Command Center, the Test page’s import history, the Tests list sorted by Finding count, exports, Triage Engine rule previews, bulk edits on the Findings list and tag filters on the Findings list are faster. The tag picker no longer slows down for users scoped to a few Assets, downstream connectors are updated once per import, and large Qualys XML reports parse in linear time.

Bug fixes:

  • (Connectors) A Coverity Discover no longer stops on a project with no name: the project is skipped with a warning, and records with a blank product name are named after their ID.
  • (Reporting) Reports show pasted screenshots. In PDF reports, long code wraps and a Finding too large for one page breaks across pages. Numeric filters work in chart blocks, previews, Triage Engine rule scopes and dashboard tiles, and a ~ in report text no longer shows a backslash before it. See Report Builder.
  • (Dashboards) An Embedded Table keeps a viewer’s saved filters after a reload, and a widget’s saved filters can be removed or cleared in the editor. The Command Center’s Add Widget dialog titles a new widget as new, and a graph taller than its tile scrolls to its top. See Customizable Dashboards.
  • (Risk Acceptance) An older Risk Acceptance that has expired reads as expired, and one that is extended expires again on its new date. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Triage Engine) A scheduled run of a disabled rule is recorded as skipped instead of successful. A Send an Email node can only address Email connections. See Scheduling Rules and Send an Email.
  • (Findings) The Remediation Center groups host Findings by the fix they need. A component name that only repeats the host’s name is ignored, and vendor advisories with no component become one upgrade per product per host. See Remediation Center.
  • (Sensei) Sensei scans no longer fail when they wait in the queue for a long time: a run is timed from when it starts, and it gets fresh source-control tokens when it starts. A clone that fails because the Git host is unreachable says so, and a scan of a Java repository analyzes only that repository’s own compiled code, or is shown as Partial when there is none. See Sensei Reference.
  • (Organizations) The change plan preview for moving an Organization lists only the rules, dashboard layouts and report schedules that refer to it. See Change Plans.
  • (Notifications) Users whose notification settings were created outside the app, such as from a fixture, receive Pro event notifications, and a user with two global notification rows gets a consistent result. See About Notifications.
  • (Integrations) A ticket template action that holds only a string literal can be saved, an action that holds only trim markers is refused when saved instead of failing later, and the template check’s messages are translated. A refused issue tracker mapping save keeps the dialog open and shows the server’s messages under their fields.
  • (API) /api/v2/findings/ honors the engagement, product and prod_type filters. The full health check no longer fails on instances missing a Location table. See DefectDojo API v2.
  • (Parsers) The Qualys XML parser skips a Finding whose QID has no glossary entry instead of failing the import.
  • (MCP) When saving the MCP server switch is refused, the switch stays on the server’s state and one message is shown. See MCP Server.
  • (Settings) Removing one rule on the Firewall Settings page no longer removes other rules for the same IP address. A deployment setting changed across a restart, such as turning API tokens off, reaches browsers that already had the app open.
  • (Tables) A dragged column keeps its width when the table redraws during the drag. See Customizing Tables.
  • (UI) Enter starts a new line in form text areas and editors. A saved setting no longer reverts to an older value from a refresh sent before the save. The gear menus on Organization and Test pages appear once the record has loaded. Numbers and dashboard text follow the app language. Message contrast, page landmarks, link names, scrolling table regions and form spacing in right-to-left languages are improved for accessibility. See Language and Localization.

Security fixes:

  • (Authorization) Report schedules are visible only to their creator and to users who can see the reports they produce. Adding a note to a Finding, Test or Engagement requires permission to add notes on it, and downloading a Risk Acceptance’s proof requires permission to view that Risk Acceptance. A revoked permission stops applying as soon as it is removed. A Triage Engine rule can name only a connection that its author and its owner may use. See Action permission charts and Node Reference.
  • (Hardening) SSO, LDAP and SMTP secrets saved on the Settings pages are stored encrypted in the database. See Single Sign-On.

Behavior changes:

  • (Permissions) Configuration Permissions, which open settings pages such as Users, Tool Types and SLA Configurations, come from roles. A role carries them in its Configuration Permissions table, and they apply when the role is held as a Global Role, directly or through a Group. A user or Group can hold several Global Roles, and they add up. The upgrade creates a role for each set of Configuration Permissions in use and adds it beside each holder’s existing Global Role, so no one loses access. See Custom RBAC Roles.
  • (Authentication) Session Age is counted from login, so a session ends when it passes, however active the user has been. After the upgrade, a signed-in session’s clock starts at its first request. See Login Settings.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Deployment) PostgreSQL stops any single statement of a web request that runs past 30 seconds under the service’s harakiri, and the request answers with a 503. Background tasks, migrations and management commands are not limited. DD_DATABASE_WEB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT, DD_DATABASE_WEB_LONG_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT and, on Docker Compose, DD_DATABASE_IMPORT_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT change the limits. See Hardware Sizing for Self-Hosted DefectDojo Pro.
  • (Deployment) SSO, LDAP and SMTP secrets saved in Settings are encrypted with DD_SECRET_KEY. To change the key, set the new one in DD_SECRET_KEY and keep the old one in DD_SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS, a comma-separated list. See Restoring a Self-Hosted Deployment.
  • (Helm) The Sensei engine finishes running scans before it shuts down, for up to sensei.shutdownGraceSeconds (300 by default), and keeps a job journal (sensei.jobJournal.enabled, on by default) so jobs interrupted by a restart are run again at once. A rollout can take up to about 5 minutes per Sensei engine pod while scans run. See DefectDojo Pro Upgrade Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

dojo-deploy 3.5.0

dojo-deploy is the new command line tool for self-hosted DefectDojo Pro. It replaces dojo-compose-cli and dojo-helm-cli: it runs their commands as dojo-deploy compose and dojo-deploy kubernetes, and adds install, upgrade, check, prereqs, verify and support-bundle. 3.5.0 is its first release. Download it from cloud.defectdojo.com/tools.

Existing installs get these changes through the update they already run (sudo -E dojo-compose-cli update-binary or dojo-helm-cli update-binary), as dojo-compose-cli 2.2.0 and dojo-helm-cli 4.1.0. Both are now legacy commands. They keep their names, commands and options, keep working, and print a short note in the terminal that links to Moving to dojo-deploy. The same run also installs dojo-deploy next to the old CLI, with the same owner, group and mode (on Docker Compose, at /usr/bin/dojo-deploy, owned by root), so moving from dojo-compose-cli 2.1.1 to 2.1.9 or dojo-helm-cli 4.0.x takes one update-binary run. If dojo-deploy cannot be installed (offline, air-gapped, or no permission), the update still succeeds, and dojo-compose-cli doctor or the next update-binary points to cloud.defectdojo.com/tools. The changes below are measured against dojo-compose-cli 2.1.9 and dojo-helm-cli 4.0.1.

Docker Compose:

  • (Compose) app restart no longer fails when nginx or the dojo container restarts during startup and then stays up. The check lasts 30 seconds. It still fails when a container exits or is killed for running out of memory, or when it is still restarting, or starts again, in the last 15 seconds.
  • (Compose) A license file that is a symbolic link is refused instead of copied. The copy beside the compose file (/opt/dojo/dojopro.lic) is written to a new file and renamed into place, so a failed copy leaves nothing half-written. app upgrade now carries that copy into the new install directory with mode 0640, owned by the service user and group.
  • (Compose) On a new host, the first command run as root creates /etc/defectdojo/compose.config with mode 0660, owned by the service user and group. Before, it was readable by every local user until first-install ran. doctor now reports /etc/defectdojo as clean on a fresh host. The file is written in one step, so a crash or full disk cannot leave it half-written, and a symbolic link, FIFO or hard link at that path is refused.
  • (Compose) Each install gets its own DD_SHOGUN_SHARED_SECRET, stored encrypted like the other service secrets. An install that uses a value DefectDojo ships gets a new one on its next start or upgrade, with a warning. A value you set yourself is kept.
  • (Compose) Stopping DefectDojo waits for the import service’s stop grace period on releases that have one. app start, app restart, app upgrade and doctor --fix add a systemd drop-in, /etc/systemd/system/defectdojo-compose.service.d/50-dojo-compose-cli-stop-timeout.conf, that sets TimeoutStopSec=4200. A value you set with systemctl edit still wins.
  • (Compose) doctor warns about more problems: a systemd stop timeout under 4200 seconds, a revoked running release, an internal CA that every install shares, unlabelled bind mounts on an SELinux host, and Docker user namespace remapping it could not check. Plain doctor still exits 0 for these. doctor --strict exits non-zero until they are fixed.
  • (Compose) app upgrade, first-install and bundle create refuse a DefectDojo Pro release that has been revoked, and “latest” skips it. The CLI reads the signed list from intel.defectdojo.com. If the list cannot be read, it warns and carries on. Air-gapped installs do not fetch it.
  • (Compose) An install older than 2.58.0 can no longer jump straight to 3.0.0 / 2.59.0 or later, which failed halfway through the database migration. Upgrade to 2.58.4 first. app upgrade also stops before changing anything when the installed or target version cannot be read, for example an install recorded as latest.
  • (Compose) A first install generates its own internal CA and service certificates. Existing installs keep theirs. The new certs rotate-internal command replaces a shared internal CA, after backing up the old files under certs/backup/.
  • (Compose) media/ belongs to the containers’ user (uid 1001), which fixes an HTTP 500 on the first scan import after an install. customizations/ is created with mode 0755 whatever the umask, so DefectDojo Pro loads its settings under a strict umask.
  • (Compose) On a host where Docker runs with SELinux enabled, the CLI loads docker-compose.selinux.yml from the deployment files, so the bind mounts are labelled and stop failing with AVC denials.
  • (Compose) With rootless Docker, the systemd unit keeps DOCKER_HOST and no longer starts the rootful Docker daemon at boot.
  • (Compose) environment print no longer crashes when the license is not at /etc/defectdojo/dojopro.lic. As root, environment print and environment remove work on an incomplete install.
  • (Compose) dojo-deploy install, dojo-deploy upgrade and dojo-deploy compose app upgrade lock the install for the whole run. A second run on the same install exits before changing anything and names the run that holds the lock.

Kubernetes:

  • (Helm) deploy status no longer prints the release’s values, which hold the license and passwords. It prints a summary like helm status does, with secrets removed. Scripts that parsed the old JSON need --output json.
  • (Helm) diag redacts Helm values, ConfigMaps and logs by default. --no-redact keeps them, but Secret data is still left out.
  • (Helm) deploy and download-artifacts refuse a revoked release, “latest” skips it, and download-artifacts --list-versions marks revoked versions. deploy status warns when the running release is revoked.
  • (Helm) New options: deploy --kubeconfig and --context, preflight --profile, and download-artifacts --image-platform and --overwrite.
  • (Helm) update-binary checks the download’s digest and size before it installs it.

New in dojo-deploy:

  • (dojo-deploy) dojo-deploy support-bundle writes one redacted support bundle for a Docker Compose or Kubernetes install. It finds the install by itself, uploads nothing, and --validate checks a bundle. See Support bundle.

item.title: October 30, 2026: v3.4.304
item.description:
New features:

  • (Connectors) Ingestion Health has its own page, Settings > Operations > Ingestion Health, listing every source of Findings: each Upstream Connector, each scheduled Triage Engine rule, and each Asset and scan type imported through the API in the last 30 days. Each row shows the last run and its result, the baseline, when the next run is expected and any open anomalies. Three anomaly kinds join the zero-Findings check: Volume Drop, Stale and Auth Failed. Each source can have its own thresholds or be snoozed, the Ingestion Health Warning notification goes out once per anomaly, and the Ingestion Health Status dashboard widget counts the sources that need attention. Requires the Ingestion Health feature flag, off by default. See Ingestion Health.

Enhancements:

  • (Connectors) A Connector shows when its next scheduled Discover or Sync will run. The Operations view labels its Type, Status and Trigger tags in the reader’s language, and a Connector save that fails because the connector service cannot be reached says so in plain words. See Managing Operations.
  • (Assets) The Open Finding Severity tile on the Asset page is one bar split by severity, with a legend across its full width and the total in the tile header, and its severity links filter correctly in every language. The Reachability Coverage panel leads with the Criticals confirmed reachable and the Criticals demoted, and shows coverage as one bar. See Assets and Reachability.
  • (Dashboards) Each dashboard tile keeps its actions in one Widget Actions menu, so its controls no longer shrink or overlap beside the title and freshness stamp. Add to Report moved into the same menu. See Customizable Dashboards.
  • (Settings) The Feature Flags page groups features by area, with an index beside the cards, an X of Y Enabled count, filters by state, and one-line descriptions that expand in place. See Feature Flags.
  • (Parsers) A Generic Findings Import JSON finding accepts a purl for its dependency, or purl_type and namespace alongside component_name, so the dependency location carries the right package type.
  • (Performance) Reimporting large reports costs less per Finding, filtering the Findings list by mitigated date and requesting ?prefetch=endpoints are faster, and updating or deleting a single Finding through the API no longer loads its related records one row at a time.

Bug fixes:

  • (Permissions) The built-in Writer role can add files to Findings, Tests, Engagements and Assets again. A Permissions dialog opened before its page finishes loading lists only that record’s members. See Set Permissions in Pro.
  • (Deduplication) After consolidating Findings, moving a tool back to As the parser groups them splits them on the next reimport, which reactivates each folded-away Finding with its locations. The first grouping change on an instance backfills existing Findings before it takes effect, so a reimport in between no longer closes Findings and opens copies. Reimporting an older Test whose Finding was folded into another keeps that Test’s location active. On the Dedupe Pools page, a Preview Re-run is kept when Add to Pool finishes, a pool created during a refresh is listed, and a delete waits for the pool’s members to load. See Deduplication Tuning and Dedupe Pools.
  • (Importers) Reimport Scan works on a Test whose scan type differs from its test type name, such as a GitLab SAST Report. With Locations enabled, a dependency too long to store is left off its Finding with a warning in the log, instead of failing the whole import. See Tests.
  • (Findings) Updating a Finding through the API returns its recalculated priority, and an update with recalculate_hash_code stores the recalculated hash and deduplicates on it. When a close is refused, Close Finding shows one message with the server’s reason, and a refused note is shown under the Note field.
  • (Tables) The On, Before, After and During filters on date-only fields match the day the viewer picked, including for viewers in a timezone ahead of the server’s. See Customizing Tables.
  • (Licensing) On an instance over its license limit, OAuth and OIDC sign-in works again, and only changes that add usage are blocked: new Findings, imports and reimports, new Assets, new users and new Connector operations. Revoking access, editing or deactivating users, and rotating tokens keep working.
  • (SSO) The SAML settings help says that the NameID picks the account a login lands on, not a mapped Username or Email. See SAML Configuration.
  • (Navigation) Every in-app walkthrough can be finished, starts on a record the user can act on, and describes what is on screen. A highlighted sidebar row stays in view when the sidebar footer grows. See In-App Walkthroughs.
  • (UI) A dashboard tile’s default title follows the reader’s language, the toggles on Priority Insights and the Asset hierarchy panel are translated, and translated column headers fit in the Regulatory Scope widget. Screen readers announce whether a popup menu is open. A switch whose change is refused, such as a policy’s Enabled switch on Settings > AI Governance Policies, flips back and shows one message. A long unbroken error wraps inside its message instead of widening the page, and the PSIRT Applies To panel keeps keyboard focus after each change. See Language and Localization.

Security fixes:

  • (Authentication) A SAML logout message that cannot be read is refused with a 400 response. See SAML Configuration.
  • (Authorization) The Risk Acceptance page acts only on notes that belong to that Risk Acceptance. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Hardening) Triage Engine Slack messages show Finding titles, Asset names and Card Facts as plain text. The Helm bootstrap scripts no longer print the admin password; they name the Secret that holds it and how to read it. The application images apply security updates to their bundled components. See Send a Slack Message and DefectDojo Pro Installation Guide (Kubernetes / Helm).

Behavior changes:

  • (Assets) Unmanaged Devices is now called Asset Discovery: the sidebar entry under Attack Surface, the page and its walkthrough, and the feature flag’s title on the Feature Flags page. Menu search still finds the page by its old name. See Asset Discovery.

item.title: October 29, 2026: v3.4.303
item.description:
New features:

  • (Compliance) A Finding’s FedRAMP Potential Agency Impact (PAIN) rating can be set, changed or cleared by hand: on Edit Finding, in Bulk Edit, and through pain_rating on the Findings API, which also accepts it when a Finding is created. The Findings list gains a PAIN column and a filter that offers Unrated. Rating needs the new Rate Potential Agency Impact (PAIN) permission, which every role that can edit Findings receives on upgrade. See Potential Agency Impact (PAIN) Ratings.
  • (Findings) My Work is one Up Next queue of everything waiting on you, grouped by deadline into Overdue, Due in 7 Days, Later, No Due Date and Waiting on Others: assigned Findings, reviews to claim or clear, Risk Acceptances about to expire, and remediation actions assigned to you. Each item has a next-step button that opens the matching form, and the queue shows as a list, a grid or a board. See My Work.
  • (Sensei) Ask Sensei answers “what should I fix first?” with fixes rather than Findings: the Root Causes that clear the most, exploited ones first, each with a Fix With Sensei button that shows the plan before Sensei opens pull requests. The panel can expand to full width or open as its own page, and a new conversation opens on a home view of what changed since your last visit and the top fixes. Ranked fixes need Root Cause Correlation. See Ask Sensei.

Enhancements:

  • (Deduplication) Matching Configuration shows each tool’s default algorithm and hash fields, and Reset to Default loads them into the form, to be saved through Review Impact like any other matching change. See Deduplication Tuning.
  • (Reporting) On Organization, Asset, Engagement, Test and Finding blocks, the Fields and Order By pickers list their fields under the same headings as that list’s Add Filter. See Report Builder.
  • (Navigation) Each control in the sidebar footer has its own shape: What’s New is one button naming the release and its unseen count, the Production/Sandbox switch is a full-width button, and the account row shows your username and email beside the alerts bell. Ask Sensei moved into the search field as an Ask button. See The Sidebar Menu.
  • (Settings) When the running release has been revoked, users who can see the Version Manager get a banner with the reason and the release to upgrade to, and the Version Manager never offers a revoked release as the latest version. See Revoked releases.
  • (API) The Findings API takes a has_sla filter: true keeps Findings that have an SLA date, false keeps those without one.

Bug fixes:

  • (Findings) SLA status agrees on every page. Today is the viewer’s date, an open Finding due today is within SLA and reads Due Today, and a mitigated Finding is judged by the date it was mitigated, so the Findings list, Finding Groups, the Insights counts and charts, and the Mitigated Within SLA column put a Finding on the same side of its due date. An open Finding Group’s SLA comes from its open Findings only. An owner assignment completes when its Finding closes, so closed Findings no longer count as open work, and a closed Finding cannot be assigned. See How SLA days are counted and Peer Review & Claiming.
  • (Deduplication) Mark as Duplicate in the Similar Findings menu refuses to mark an open Finding as a duplicate of a mitigated one, and shows one message with the reason. Consolidating historical churn no longer merges distinct Findings: it orders Findings by import instead of by timestamp, so backdated scan dates cannot chain Findings that were open at the same time, and it leaves out false positive, risk accepted and out of scope Findings. See Similar Findings and Location Drift Matching.
  • (Tables) Sort offers custom fields on the Assets, Organizations, Engagements and Tests lists, as the Findings list already did, so the grid view can sort by them; multi-select custom fields are not offered on any list. A column filter that has not been applied yet is left alone when settings sync in the background. Toolbar icon buttons match the height of the fields beside them, toolbar labels give way to icons instead of overlapping on narrow windows, and a Tags cell shows the whole tags that fit and folds the rest into +N. See Customizing Tables.
  • (Dashboards) A dashboard tile’s header stays on one row with a readable title, while viewing and while editing, including beside a stale or failed freshness stamp. See Customizable Dashboards.
  • (Locations) Sorting the Locations list by Status, including in a Finding’s affected-locations view, works instead of failing to load. See Locations Overview.
  • (Importers) Reimport Scan on a Test keeps Submit disabled until the Test’s details load, so a quick submit no longer fails validation on fields that cannot be edited. See Tests.
  • (Settings) The Version Manager answers normally on a new instance’s first page load instead of returning a server error. See Upgrading DefectDojo Pro (On-Premise).

item.title: October 28, 2026: v3.4.302
item.description:
New features:

  • (AI) AI Guardrails checks every Claude Code prompt and tool call against a policy you control. A policy can block a prompt that holds personal data, redact secrets from file contents and command output before the model sees them, stop or ask about a risky command, or log a match. Developers get the policy through Claude Code’s managed settings, and each checked call is listed under Prompt Activity. Create Starter Policy on Settings > AI Guardrails adds a baseline policy in monitor mode. Requires the AI Inventory and Governance feature flag, off by default, and only superusers can see or change guardrails. See AI Guardrails for Claude Code.
  • (Connectors) Ingestion Health flags a Connector whose Syncs keep succeeding with zero Findings while it usually imports some. The Connector’s tile reads Returned 0 Findings Against a Baseline of n, where the baseline is the median Findings per Sync over the last 30 days, and a user who can edit the Connector can acknowledge it with a reason that stays on record. The next Sync that imports Findings clears it. Requires the Ingestion Health feature flag, off by default. See Ingestion Health.

Enhancements:

  • (Assets) Every count card at the top of the Asset page shows what makes up its total, plus one figure for what needs attention, which turns amber or red above zero: open, closed and overdue Engagements; last scanned, imports in the last 30 days and new Findings for Tests; direct, indirect and past-SLA Findings; and vulnerable, not vulnerable and critical Endpoints or Locations. See Assets.
  • (Tables) Sort in the filter bar takes any number of sort levels. Drag a level by its grip, or press Up or Down, to reorder it, and Reset to Default clears the sort. On the Findings, Assets, Organizations, Engagements and Tests lists, the Columns picker and Sort list their fields under the same headings as Add Filter. See Customizing Tables.
  • (UI) Icons in the sidebar, top bar, breadcrumbs, table headers and buttons are drawn in a quieter tone than the labels beside them.
  • (Performance) Opening a Finding no longer runs a query for each finding group in its Test, and API requests with ?prefetch=test load a Test’s finding groups and their Jira issues once.

Bug fixes:

  • (Triage Engine) Switching a rule’s schedule from Single Run to Repeated Run starts it at the top of the hour, and the minute can no longer be cleared, so the rule saves instead of failing with an invalid cron expression. This applies to every schedule dialog. See Scheduling Rules.
  • (Reporting) A report left Processing past its time limit, for example because its worker stopped, is marked failed with the timed-out reason. In the template editor, a role with Report Template Add but not Edit can preview a new block and see its chart keys. A template block entry with no block is refused with a 400 instead of a server error. See Report Builder.
  • (Deduplication) Following a completed Locations migration, Findings in different files are no longer marked duplicates of each other. The upgrade recomputes the stored hashes; Findings already marked duplicate are not changed. Marking an open Finding as a duplicate of a mitigated one is refused, as automatic deduplication already does, Set as original works on a duplicate that has lost its original, and deleting a single Finding no longer deadlocks with the duplicate cleanup. See About Deduplication.
  • (Importers) Reimport no longer adds a newly reported host to a Finding marked false positive, out of scope or risk accepted for a different host. An import that loses its database connection names the database error and its SQLSTATE in the error response. See Reimport Deduplication.
  • (Findings) Add Finding From Template fills the description, mitigation, impact, CVSS v3 vector and vulnerability IDs from the template, not only its title, severity, CWE and tags.
  • (Assets) An Asset’s Technologies tab lists only that Asset’s technologies. See Assets.
  • (Settings) A new SLA configuration starts with the default day counts filled in, so it can be saved with only a name. See Assign Priority, Risk and SLAs.
  • (Sensei) Agent targets can be onboarded from the hub’s Add Accounts menu, under Add Agent Targets. The item is disabled with the reason when the license has no agent-target quota or the quota is used up. The menu’s connect-first items read Connect a Source-Control Provider First and Connect a Cloud Provider First in every language. See AI Agent Red Teaming.
  • (Licensing) A replacement license can be saved on the License Manager page while the instance is over its license limit.
  • (Tables) A filter being edited is no longer cleared when the table’s settings refresh in the background.
  • (API) The API token page shows the current key after the token is regenerated in another tab or reset by an administrator, and hides token controls when the instance has API tokens turned off. Concurrent requests for the OpenAPI schema no longer fail with a server error, and a request larger than the upload limits answers 413 instead of 500. See DefectDojo API v2.
  • (UI) On a multi-step create form, Next is the main button until every step has been reached, and the held Submit explains why it is disabled. A user, environment, or Asset platform, lifecycle or origin that cannot be deleted says how many records still refer to it and which kinds, instead of listing each one. A webhook receiver’s URL and secret buttons wrap at phone width.

Upgrade notes:

  • (Deployment) On instances with a completed Locations migration, the upgrade recomputes deduplication hashes, which can lengthen the migration. DD_REHASH_MIGRATION_WORKERS sets how many processes run it, up to four by default. See Upgrading DefectDojo Pro (On-Premise).

item.title: October 27, 2026: v3.4.301
item.description:
Enhancements:

  • (UI) Each tab in a page layout’s tab group can be set to hide when it has nothing to show, so a record no longer opens on an empty tab. The option is on each tab row in the Tabs widget’s Configure Widget dialog. Tiles on detail pages and dashboards now share the header band, title and spacing of the section cards around them. See Customizing Page Layouts.
  • (Performance) The dashboard priority histogram, Top-N records and Command Center tallies read less data. See Command Center.

Bug fixes:

  • (SSO) Signing in through an OAuth or OIDC provider works again. In v3.4.300 these sign-ins returned a server error once a provider was chosen. SAML sign-in was not affected. See Single Sign-On.
  • (Importers) A background import that fails leaves its Test’s status at Failed until the next import, instead of reporting Processed, and the status reads Post Processing - Deduplication while deduplication runs. See DefectDojo API v2.
  • (Reporting) A report that reaches the time limit while drawing a chart, a widget or an image fails with the time-out reason, instead of staying Processing or completing with a placeholder. A refused template save names the Template Blocks and Theme fields the way the form does. See Report Builder.
  • (Dashboards) The Command Center finishes loading on large datasets, because a scheduled refresh waits for the previous load to finish. On the Insights pages, the filter bar keeps its own height and its “Some data may be hidden” warning stays in view. See Command Center and Pro Metrics Overview.
  • (API) A 400 response raised by a model or importer check reads as plain sentences. A delete blocked by other records answers 409 with how many records still refer to it and which kinds they are, instead of listing each one. See DefectDojo API v2.

item.title: October 26, 2026: v3.4.300
item.description:
NOTE: v3.4.300 was revoked: Signing in through an OAuth or OIDC provider returns a server error. SAML sign-in is not affected. Upgrade to v3.4.301.

New features:

  • (Findings) A Finding’s Title, Tags, Severity, Assignees, Planned Remediation Date and Description can be changed on the Finding page itself, without opening the Edit Finding form. Changes are held until you save, several fields can be changed and saved together, and a change someone else made since the page loaded is never overwritten. The same in-place editing is on the Engagement and Asset pages. Requires the Inline Editing feature flag, on by default. See Editing Findings.
  • (Notifications) The bell in the sidebar footer opens a notification inbox: unread alerts grouped by the record they are about, with All, Mentions, Assigned, Watching and System tabs, the option to mute a record, and read state carried to the Alerts Page. The counts refresh on their own, and Load Older pages through the rest. The inbox is now generally available. See About Notifications.
  • (API) Service users are API-only accounts with no email or password that never sign in, each holding one token shown once at creation, and authorized through memberships, groups and a global role on their own page. Requires the Service Users feature flag, off by default. See Service Users.
  • (Deduplication) Each scan type can set how its Findings are grouped: as the parser produces them (the default), one Finding per location, or one Finding per vulnerability, where every location of a vulnerability becomes one Finding that stays open until each location is fixed. The location-based options need the Locations feature. See Deduplication Tuning.
  • (Triage Engine) Rules can be exported, imported and restored: move a set of rules between instances with a compatibility check, restore an earlier version of a rule, and manage rules through the API. See Sharing and Versions.
  • (Connectors) Unmanaged device discovery lists the devices your EDR sees on the network with no agent of their own, as CrowdStrike Falcon Discover and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint report them. Each device is a candidate and becomes neither an Asset nor a Finding on its own. Requires the Unmanaged Devices feature flag, off by default, turned on per connection with Report Unmanaged Devices. See Unmanaged Devices.

Enhancements:

  • (Connectors) A connector’s label can be renamed without re-homing its Engagements. See Add or Edit Upstream Connectors.
  • (Connectors) Tenable groups records by asset and adds WAS scan-configuration grouping and a WAS tag filter, Checkmarx One tags Findings with their triage state and exploitable path and carries their comments, Qualys sets each Finding’s date from when it was first found, and Wiz reports a runtime reachability verdict. Connector-owned tags and the triage comment stay current on reimport, and a connector whose filters match nothing shows a warning.
  • (Jira) Findings can be unlinked from Jira in a bulk edit. See Bulk Editing Findings.
  • (Triage Engine) Rules can be scoped to hosts, IP addresses and CIDR networks.
  • (Dashboards) The Count and Graph widgets can measure unique CWEs or unique vulnerability IDs instead of rows, such as unique CWEs by severity for one Asset, and roll the measure up across child Assets. See Customizable Dashboards.
  • (API) A new API exports an Asset and everything under it as a manifest plus an NDJSON stream. See Product export.
  • (Locations) Each location reference records the Test that reported it. See Locations Overview.
  • (Navigation) The sidebar footer has an account row and a single row of icon buttons (alerts, What’s New, Ask Sensei and the Production/Sandbox switch), and the account menu holds the language and light/dark choices. The What’s New panel remembers the release you have seen, per account, and Hide Walkthroughs is on the lightbulb’s list. See The Sidebar Menu.
  • (Settings) The All Settings page is compacted into group cards. See The Sidebar Menu.
  • (Threat Intelligence) A Finding’s Threat Intelligence tile shows pending enrichment and KEV status. See EPSS / KEV.
  • (Performance) The Findings and Engagements lists no longer run a query per row, tag filters match with EXISTS instead of a DISTINCT join, bulk deletes and an import’s finding groups run as one set-based operation, import and reimport requests cost a fixed few queries, and dashboard tile counts, the import list and a user’s History tab read less. Connector configuration saves and deletes cost a fixed few queries.

Bug fixes:

  • (Findings) A Finding keeps its Locations when the Pro UI edit form is saved.
  • (Risk Acceptance) A Finding stays in a single risk acceptance when one is reinstated or approved, including under concurrent writes. Reinstating leaves out Findings accepted elsewhere since the expiry, and Jira is told after the change commits. See Risk Acceptances.
  • (Reporting) Report failure reasons are translated, and a report that reaches the time limit says so. A template’s block ordering is checked when it is saved, with a missing sort field named under Order By, the template editor is tidied, and Add Existing Block follows the permission that saves the template. See Report Builder.
  • (Importers) The import form’s help is corrected for Scan Date (the mitigated date), asynchronous import and a disabled Close Old Findings, and the Do Not Reactivate option on reimport is explained. See Add Findings form.
  • (Parsers) The generic importer rejects a field value wider than its Finding column with a 400, instead of failing the import without a clear reason. See Generic Findings Import.
  • (Connectors) The GitHub connector resolves repositories by URL and owner/name instead of display name, Cycode accepts numeric project IDs, and Qualys WAS leaves an empty filter block out of searches that have no criteria. See GitHub.
  • (Sensei) A pasted repository access token no longer outranks the repository’s connection and can be replaced or removed, reachability scans fetch private Go modules from the same organization, and a fix is applied to every active code location of a Finding in one change. See Fixing Findings with Sensei.
  • (Compliance) The CRA scope widget counts every Finding in scope, and the CRA evidence pack’s support-period obligation reads each Asset’s Support Period End. See CRA Article 14 Reporting.
